detail.longDescription:
Every page of a PDF appears as a thumbnail that can be reordered, copied, deleted, or rotated with a single drag. Select multiple pages at once and pull them into a new PDF, or drop in pages pulled from a completely different document sitting on the same device. Reordering a hundred page contract takes the same two taps as fixing a five page handout, regardless of how the original file was put together in the first place.

A search by meaning locates pages instead of exact words, so a request like all pages with tables or pages that mention the contract returns results without scrolling through every sheet by hand. Useful for scanned reports where page numbers alone say nothing about what is actually sitting inside them, especially once a document runs past a hundred pages long overall.

Rotate or resize groups of pages together instead of repeating the same adjustment one page at a time. A stack of mixed portrait and landscape scans becomes consistent in a single pass, without opening each page on its own screen. Every edit produces a new file. The source PDF stays untouched on the device, so a page removed by mistake is never actually gone for good, and nothing has to be reconstructed from scratch. Thumbnails in, a clean file out, nothing lost along the way, nothing left to guess about afterward.
